chapter: Other Philadelphia work and the union
title: Charlie Gaines and Charlie James gigs in Philadelphia
summary: Waters clarifies that a trumpeter was better known rather than better, identifies Charlie Gaines, and recalls commercial gigs with Gaines and with Charlie James of the Black union.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You were mentioning a trumpet player in Philadelphia you said was famous who you knew?
Well, I mean, not Bill Lee -
No, no no, you said -
Another one -
You said Bill Lee had, there was a guy who became more famous than Bill Lee.
Ah, it was a trumpet player, but I can't forget his, I forget his name.
You called him Charles the other day, Charlie Gaines?
Oh no, not - more famous, no, I didn't say famous, I didn't say famous musically - no, we got it wrong there, Phil. I didn't say more famous musically, I said more known.
Uh huh.
That's the word I used. I said very well -
[ ] Charlie Gaines -
Very - that's Charlie Gaines. I said very well known, and then you said Charlie Gaines.
Right.
And I says 'Yes, that's it'. See, that's where, I didn't say more famous or played more trumpet, I says more well known, he's one of the first ones -
But he was in the Philadelphia area -
Oh sure, I worked with him too. Now see, there you are, see. I worked with Charlie also during that period, if -
Jazz gigs.
Well, Charlie - we had, there was some -
Some jazz, some dance -
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
Yeah, yeah. It was commercial, but a little better than the dancing -
Than the one you left to go with Charlie Miller -
Yeah, I worked many gigs with Willie - I wonder if he's still living now. He'd be quite old though, I guess, for the game [?] -
Charlie James -

Charlie James, he was associated with the union down there at one time in Philadelphia, the negro union. Yeah, that's another one, see how it comes to me, I can't, see - because I didn't work that long. You see, that's where, that's where you can get me mixed -
